land.text: Algeciras and the southern coast around it: 'in what is now southern Spain and Gibraltar'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Caliphate of Cordoba'; the Hammudids received Algeciras from Sulayman ibn al-Hakam (undated).

successors.note: 1055: Seville takes Algeciras. 'In 1055 al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad, lord of Seville, appeared under Algeciras' walls, forcing Muhammad to leave the taifa' (the infobox says 'Conquered by the Taifa of Seville: 1058'; the Abbad II page 'Algeciras (1055)'). The Almoravids received the city from al-Mu'tamid in July 1086 and the Almohads took it in 1147 (Abd al-Mu'min page), both in the Seville, Almoravid and Almohad dossiers.

capitals.name: Algeciras (al-Jazīra al-Khaḍrāʾ)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Algeciras' (undated). The dot is drawn only while the state exists, 1013-1055. A second taifa of Algeciras in 1147-1168 is not supported by any page (see keyframes 1147 and 1152) and is dropped.

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim
rulers.note: Infobox 1035–1048; the body says he 'was proclaimed emir of Algeciras' in 1039 and that Algeciras was annexed to Málaga in 1035.

rulers.name: Al-Qasim al-Wathiq
rulers.note: Infobox 1048–1058; the body has Muhammad forced out in 1055 when al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad appeared under the walls, so the list is cut at 1055, the end of the dossier.

correction.text: Algeciras and the Campo de Gibraltar without the Málaga country

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The taifa was created in 1013' (body); Cliopatria starts in 1028. The page gives no extent and names only 'southern Spain and Gibraltar'. Cliopatria's 1028 shape (8,680 km2) cannot be applied back: about 1,500 km2 of it lie in Morocco (6 of 33 grid cells; the bbox runs to 35.58N) and 18 of its 33 cells lie in Málaga province, which the Taifa of Málaga held ('Málaga: 1026–1057/1058', Taifa article; the caliphate dossier gives Málaga province to that taifa in 1026). The city and its district are drawn instead (confidence 1 on the extent). Revised after review: the first version only removed Morocco.

correction.text: Algeciras and the Campo de Gibraltar without the Málaga country

keyframe_review.note: 8,680 km2 on shapes.csv (bbox 35.58-37.13N), of which about 1,500 km2 lie in Morocco (6 of 33 grid cells; an earlier note said 2,700) and 18 of 33 cells in Málaga province. The page places the taifa 'in what is now southern Spain and Gibraltar' (infobox 'Today part of: Spain, Gibraltar') and says Algeciras was 'annexed ... to the taifa of Málaga in 1035' and that Muhammad ibn al-Qasim 'was proclaimed emir of Algeciras' in 1039, so Algeciras stood apart from Málaga and the Málaga country is not its land. Only the city and its district are kept (the ledger carries the 1035 and 1039 changes); Cliopatria's Taifa of Ceuta is a separate shape from 1066. Revised after review: the first version kept the Málaga part.

correction.text: Algeciras and the Campo de Gibraltar without the Málaga country; shape replaced, holds 1040-1055

keyframe_review.note: 6,000 km2 on shapes.csv, but on the gazetteer grid 15 of its 21 cells lie in Málaga province and only 5 in Cádiz: the shape is mostly the Málaga hinterland, not Algeciras (Seville's own 1056 shape does not hold that land either: it overlaps this shape only in the 5 Cádiz cells). It is replaced by the city and its district. The first life ends in 1055 ('In 1055 al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad, lord of Seville, appeared under Algeciras' walls, forcing Muhammad to leave the taifa'; the infobox says 1058), not 1065. The infobox gives no area. Revised after review: the first version passed the shape as 'right for the taifa'.

correction.text: not a taifa: Seville's land to July 1086, an Almoravid base after

keyframe_review.note: 3,718 km2 on shapes.csv; on the gazetteer grid 12 of its 14 cells lie in Málaga province, none in Cádiz, and Algeciras is not inside (the shape is the Antequera and Coín country, plausibly the Zirid Taifa of Málaga, 'Málaga: ... 1073–1090 (to Almoravids)' in the Taifa article). No page opened has a Taifa of Algeciras in 1085-1093: Seville held Algeciras from 1055 and al-Mu'tamid surrendered it to the Almoravids in July 1086 ('Ibn Tashfin demanded that Algeciras be surrendered to him so he could use it as a base'). The shape is not a taifa of Algeciras; the Seville dossier carries the July 1086 loss and its 1085 correction subtracts the city's district.

4,740 km2 on shapes.csv; on the gazetteer grid 16 of its 18 cells lie in Málaga province, none in Cádiz, and Algeciras is 36 km outside it. The Abd al-Mu'min page has the Almohads capture the city in this very year: 'In 1147 Abd al-Mu'min sent a military force led by another Almoravid defector, Abu Ishaq Barraz, who captured Algeciras and Tarifa before moving west to Niebla, Badajoz, and the Algarve' (page read again 2026-10-25; the almohad-caliphate dossier has the 1147 gain and the almoravid-dynasty dossier the loss). The Taifa article's second-period list has 'Málaga: 1145–1153 (to Almohads)' and no Algeciras. The shape is Málaga's second taifa or Almohad land, not a Taifa of Algeciras. Revised after review: the first version kept it as ok with a confidence-1 second taifa.

correction.text: not a taifa of Algeciras: Algeciras and Tarifa were Almoravid until the Almohads took them in 1147; the shape lies in Málaga province

keyframe_review.note: 4,740 km2, the identical shape as 1147 (1152-1168). Same finding: it does not contain Algeciras and lies in Málaga province; the Taifa article's second-period list gives Málaga 1145-1153 and no Algeciras, and the Abd al-Mu'min page has the Almohads take Algeciras and Tarifa in 1147. Nothing opened explains why Cliopatria draws a shape here to 1168. Revised after review.

correction.text: not a taifa of Algeciras: the same Málaga-province shape as 1147-1151 (Taifa article 'Málaga: 1145–1153'); Algeciras itself was Almohad from 1147

ledger.note: 1013: the Taifa of Algeciras is created under the Hammudids. 'The taifa was created in 1013', after the Caliphate began to break up 'after 1009'; 'The first king of Algeciras was al-Qasim al-Ma'mun, who later was also caliph.' The lead and infobox date the taifa 1035–1058 instead, and Cliopatria starts in 1028. Region revised after review: the first version drew Cliopatria's 1040 shape, which is mostly Málaga province.
1035: Algeciras is annexed to Málaga. 'Yahya al-Mu'tali, a cousin, annexed Algeciras to the taifa of Málaga in 1035.' The infobox, by contrast, starts Muhammad ibn al-Qasim's reign in 1035.
1039: Algeciras is independent again. 'In 1039 Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, son of al-Qasim, was proclaimed emir of Algeciras.' The page does not say how Málaga's rule ended.

1055: Seville takes Algeciras. 'In 1055 al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad, lord of Seville, appeared under Algeciras' walls, forcing Muhammad to leave the taifa'; the city page: 'In 1055 Emir Al-Mutadid of Seville drove the Berbers from Algeciras'. The infobox says 'Conquered by the Taifa of Seville: 1058'.

1055: the taifa ends when Seville takes the city. 'In 1055 al-Mu'tamid ibn Abbad, lord of Seville, appeared under Algeciras' walls, forcing Muhammad to leave the taifa'; the infobox puts the conquest at 1058. The land passes to Seville (the 1055 gain of the Seville dossier); the Almoravids hold it from July 1086 and the Almohads from 1147.

wars.name: Málaga's annexation of Algeciras
wars.outcome: Yahya al-Mu'tali of Málaga annexed Algeciras in 1035; Muhammad ibn al-Qasim was proclaimed emir of Algeciras in 1039.
wars.note: The page does not say how it was won or lost; the infobox gives Muhammad's reign from 1035.

wars.name: Abbadid conquest of Algeciras
wars.outcome: Seville took Algeciras: Muhammad was forced out in 1055 and the infobox puts the conquest at 1058.
wars.note: The Algeciras page has no battle, only the appearance under the walls.

certainty.note: The pages name the city and the coast, not boundaries; the district drawn is a 30 km radius round Algeciras, my reading.

notes: (1) Start/end: the lead, infobox and city page say 1035–1058, the body 'created in 1013'; I take 1013 (the body) as the birth and 1055 (Seville appears under the walls) as the end, 1058 being the infobox's. (2) Contradiction inside the page: annexed to Málaga in 1035 but Muhammad ibn al-Qasim's reign starts 1035 in the infobox and he is proclaimed in 1039 in the body; the ledger follows the body. (3) Revised after review (2026-10-25): every Cliopatria 'Taifa of Algeciras' shape is mostly Málaga province (grid cells in Málaga province: 18 of 33 in 1028, 15 of 21 in 1040, 12 of 14 in 1085, 16 of 18 in 1147-1168) and the 1028 shape also holds about 1,500 km2 of Morocco; only the 1040 shape touches Cádiz province (5 cells). The first version drew those shapes; the dossier now draws Algeciras and a 30 km radius (the bay and the Campo de Gibraltar). (4) Cliopatria's 1085-1093 shape is not a taifa and does not contain Algeciras (see the keyframe); the Seville dossier carries the July 1086 loss to the Almoravids; the Almoravid dossier has no Algeciras gain in 1086 (only the 1147 loss). (5) The second taifa of 1147-1168 is dropped: the Abd al-Mu'min page has the Almohads capture Algeciras and Tarifa in 1147, the Taifa article's second-period list has Málaga 1145-1153 and no Algeciras, and the shapes lie in Málaga province. The dossier therefore ends in 1055 with the successor Seville; the two ledger events of the second period (confidence 1) were deleted. Cliopatria's 1147-1168 rows probably belong to a second-period Taifa of Málaga (counterpart dossier needed, below). (6) Taifa of Málaga (Hammudid then Zirid, first period 1026–1057/1058 and 1073–1090, second period 1145–1153) has no dossier: Cliopatria has no row of that name, and its land is drawn under the Algeciras name. (7) The infobox gives no area; shapes compared by size, bbox and gazetteer overlay only. (8) The Hammudid caliphs al-Qasim al-Ma'mun and Yahya al-Mu'tali ruled at Córdoba and Málaga; their pages were not opened. (9) Seville's dossier holds the 1055 gain.
